title: Watch: Ceddanne Rafaela hits home runs in back-to-back at-bats
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela hit back-to-back home runs in his first two at-bats against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Rafaela's homers came off Dodgers pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto, tying the game in the third inning.
Rafaela has hit three home runs in the series, bringing his season total to 14 at Dodger Stadium.

title: Red Sox reportedly attempted to acquire shortstop Elly De La Cruz, turned down by Reds
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: The Red Sox proposed a prospects-based trade for the Reds' shortstop Elly De La Cruz, but the deal was rejected.
Boston acquired Curtis Mead for second base, but his injury has left the team seeking additional middle infield support.
Boston is hesitant to trade top prospect Franklin Arias and is pursuing an impactful shortstop before the trade deadline.

title: Drake Maye says his shoulder ‘feels great’ as Patriots training camp continues
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye reports his shoulder feels great after an injury impacted his Super Bowl LX performance.
New England adds A.J. Brown to their offense; Brown is adapting well to the Patriots' playbook, per Maye.
Maye confident in new partnership with Brown ahead of 2026-27 season, with training camp underway in Foxborough.

title: If July’s stretch of dominance wasn’t enough, the Red Sox’ win Friday proved they’re plenty capable of a postseason run
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: The Boston Red Sox defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 5-4 on Friday night despite key injuries.
Ceddanne Rafaela and Andruw Monasterio were pivotal in flipping a 4-3 deficit to a 5-4 win.
Red Sox's recent performance suggests strong postseason potential as they approach the trade deadline.

title: Red Sox fend off Dodgers, 9-4, in grindy series opener
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela's seventh-inning home run lifted Boston Red Sox over Los Angeles Dodgers 9-4 in their series opener.
Brayan Bello pitched four scoreless innings in relief, maintaining a 0.69 ERA after struggling as a starter.
Red Sox ended July with a franchise-best 21 wins, securing a .840 winning percentage for the month.

title: Gabe Jacas makes his Patriots debut and other takeaways from Day 7 of training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Drake Maye had a mixed performance during Patriots training camp, completing 8-of-11 passes and throwing an interception.
Gabe Jacas, a 2026 second-round pick, made his practice debut in a limited capacity after recovering from a knee procedure.
Undrafted free agent Tanner Arkin gained recognition for his blocking skills, earning reps with the first-team unit at Patriots camp.

title: Mass. to be 4th state to roll out EBT chip cards to curb fraud
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Massachusetts launches chip-enabled EBT cards statewide to combat fraud and theft of SNAP benefits.
Nearly 1 million residents depend on SNAP benefits via EBT cards, accepted at 5,500 retailers.
Recipients must activate new cards within 60 days, as state updates retailer payment systems.

title: Boston is now offering ‘pet certificates’ for couples who wed at City Hall
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Boston City Hall now offers 'pet certificates' for couples marrying at the venue, officially recognizing pets in the union.
Mayor Michelle Wu announced the pet certificate program, which involves a playful ceremony by the Boston Registrar.
Couples can contact the Boston Registry Division at 617-635-4175 or email [email protected] to request a pet certificate.

title: Kevin Nealon discusses Conan, Dunkin’, SNL and more ahead of local shows
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Kevin Nealon is performing in Boston and Portsmouth, New Hampshire, promoting his comedy special 'Loose in the Crotch.'
Nealon discusses his social media presence, likening his humorous tweets to working through material for stand-up.
Nealon, a former SNL cast member, reminisces about sketches and his collaborations with Dana Carvey and Adam Sandler.

title: Red Sox’ Willson Contreras leaves game after scary HBP vs. Dodgers
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Willson Contreras hit in the helmet by a 95 MPH pitch from Dodgers' Will Klein, removed for precautionary reasons.
Contreras, Red Sox's leading hitter, replaced defensively after the hit; team announced tests so far show no issues.
Manager Chad Tracy unsure of Contreras's return timeline, awaiting further assessment on Saturday morning.
